Subject: Post-call: Compute reservation & isolation — Aperture Labs alignment & next milestones

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the 40-minute call this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and suggested next steps so everyone has the same view. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of customer goals / constraints
- Target app: low-latency multi-tenant inference for clinical triage workflows (NLP + short-form summarization).
- Latency SLO: p95 generation <= 120ms for 128-token responses, with some spikes acceptable for long batches.
- Throughput estimate: steady 4M tokens/day initially; peak bursts ~2x.
- Isolation requirement: PHI workflows require tenant isolation. Primary ask is a dedicated pool or single-tenant reservation behind a VPC endpoint.
- Compliance: Aperture needs audit logs and key management; SOC2 evidence will be requested during procurement.

Primary pain points discussed
1) Unpredictable tail latency on current shared endpoints during live testing.
2) Cost volatility with burst traffic on cloud-hosted managed endpoints.
3) Procurement needs a clear MOP (runbook) and SLA wording before procurement signs off.

Redwood recommended architecture (what we proposed on the call)
- Dedicated capacity: a reserved pool of GPUs (recommend starting with 8x A100-80GB-equivalent slots) to meet steady throughput and minimize noisy-neighbor tail latency.
- Isolation: tenant-isolated pool with optional per-customer VM placement and VPC peering for PHI traffic.
- Burst policy: configured burst capacity (20% additional) and automated fallback to a lower-latency smaller model when reserved pool is saturated.
- Observability: token-level latency and cost dashboards + audit logs for all requests.

Timing & milestones (proposal)
- Technical deep-dive (ops + infra): schedule week of Apr 19 — goal: finalize pool sizing and network requirements.
- MOP + SLA draft shared: Apr 16 (attached initial MOP draft).
- Procurement review & SOC2 evidence: Apr 23–27.
- Target provisioning of reserved pool (if contract signed): mid-May.

Open questions we asked you to confirm
- Final throughput forecast (3-month horizon) so we can validate sizing.
- Is PHI required for all endpoints or only a subset of the workload?
- Procurement contact and preferred procurement cadence for a PO vs. contract.

Attachments attached to this message: Aperture_Metrics_Snapshot.xlsx (metrics export you shared), Redwood_MOP_Draft.pdf (initial runbook / roll out plan).

Next actions (owner / due)
- Soojin: send this recap and MOP (done) — due Apr 10.
- Aperture: confirm 3-month throughput and PHI scope — requested by Apr 15.
- Redwood(Ben/Jordan): schedule technical deep-dive and prepare a cost ballpark for 8x and 16x reserved configurations — by Apr 16.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
